limitations: Targeted visual and story-state checks, not engine/collision/physical-safety or native-sprite certification.
Exact untouched-pixel preservation after generation is not claimed.
Consent, identity disclosure, bed availability, paid wages and successful arrival still require actual scoped state checks.

findings.finding: Public root kitchen and private robe room are clearly separated. Modest roots and waiting bowl are visible; the uncut blue robe, closed keepsake chest and closed rear cupboard do not disclose a name, political identity or completed sale. The small removed worker seat-token is not unambiguously identifiable. Shears lie open but no cutting action or new cut is shown. The kitchen front gate is closed, although the outside public alley continues around the queue/counter; do not turn it into a locked ordinary-return condition. Private appraisal remains authorized per item, and neither garment quality nor decorative food stock proves nobility, sale permission or available economic resources.

Two open reception doors face a snowy outward road and paved city-side lane, with closed ledger, single counter token and unboarded bundle. No beds or departure convoy is invented. Separate stay-in-city room has an open street return, lamp, key and token, without a cure or rescue celebration. Extra wall papers carry decorative unreadable marks: no specific names can be read, but these surfaces must not become public passenger lists or addresses when implemented. Keep destination and care-transfer information limited to authorized receiving purposes. Closed ledger does not prove actual bed capacity or completed arrival; a lit window is no evidence of whole-city safety.

overall: 83 and 85 preserve pending private appraisal and voluntary stay/leave concepts; decorative wall notices must not expose reception identities. Original 84 and character sheet 86 not visually reviewed in this pass.
